court: European Court of Human Rights, Grand Chamber

facts.text: Since approximately 1985, serious disturbances have raged in the South-East of Turkey between the security forces and the members of the PKK (Workers' Party of Kurdistan).

anchor.surface_text: Since approximately 1985, serious disturbances have raged in the South-East of Turkey between the security forces and the members of the PKK (Workers' Party of Kurdistan).

facts.text: According to the Government, the confrontation has claimed the lives of 4,036 civilians and 3,884 members of the security forces.

anchor.surface_text: This confrontation has so far, according to the Government, claimed the lives of 4,036 civilians and 3,884 members of the security forces.

facts.text: A large number of villages, estimated at more than 1,000, have been destroyed and evacuated during this conflict.

anchor.surface_text: It appears from information submitted by the applicants and by the amicus curiae that a large number of villages, estimated at more than 1,000, have been destroyed and evacuated during this conflict

facts.text: Since 1987, ten of the eleven provinces of south-eastern Turkey have been subjected to emergency rule which was in force at the time of the facts complained of.

anchor.surface_text: Since 1987, ten of the eleven provinces of south-eastern Turkey have been subjected to emergency rule which was in force at the time of the facts complained of.

facts.text: The applicants were residents in the village of Kelekçi in the Dicle district of the province of Diyarbakir, an area with intense PKK terrorist activity.

anchor.surface_text: The applicants (see paragraph 1 above), Turkish nationals, were residents in the village of Kelekçi in the Dicle district of the province of Diyarbakir.  The village of Kelekçi and the surrounding areas have been the centre of intense PKK terrorist activity.

facts.text: The PKK launched serious attacks on Kelekçi on 17 or 18 July 1992, killing three villagers and wounding three others.

anchor.surface_text: It is undisputed that the PKK launched serious attacks on Kelekçi on 17 or 18 July 1992, and the neighbouring village of Bogazköy on 1 November 1992.  As a result of the first attack, three Kelekçi villagers were killed and three others wounded.

facts.text: On 1 November 1992, the PKK attacked the Bogazköy gendarme station, destroying it, killing one gendarme and injuring eight others.

anchor.surface_text: The second attack on 1 November 1992 was directed at the Bogazköy gendarme station, which was destroyed, with one gendarme being killed and eight others injured.

facts.text: After the attacks, security forces were reinforced in the area and extensive searches were carried out for terrorists.

anchor.surface_text: Thereafter security forces were reinforced in the area and extensive searches were carried out for terrorists.

facts.text: Applicants alleged that on 10 November 1992, State security forces attacked Kelekçi, burnt nine houses including their homes, and forced immediate evacuation of the entire village.

anchor.surface_text: The applicants alleged that on 10 November 1992 State security forces launched an attack on the village of Kelekçi, burnt nine houses, including their homes, and forced the immediate evacuation of the entire village.

facts.text: The Government denied these allegations, contending that the houses had been set on fire by the PKK and that no soldiers had entered Kelekçi on 10 November 1992.

anchor.surface_text: The Government categorically denied these allegations, contending that the houses had been set on fire by the PKK.  Initially they stated that the village had merely been searched and that no damage had been caused.  Subsequently, it was maintained that no soldiers had entered Kelekçi on 10 November 1992, and, if they had been in the vicinity, they had stopped on the outskirts of the village to take a rest.

facts.text: On 6 April 1993, houses in Kelekçi were set on fire and the village was almost completely destroyed; it is disputed whether terrorists or security forces caused this destruction.

anchor.surface_text: On 6 April 1993 houses in Kelekçi were set on fire and the village was almost completely destroyed.  It is disputed, however, whether this destruction was caused by terrorists or by security forces.

facts.text: The Commission established that nine houses, including those of the applicants, were destroyed or seriously damaged by fire not long after the attack on 1 November 1992, accepting the date as 10 November 1992.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission established that nine houses, including those of the applicants, were destroyed or seriously damaged by fire not long after the attack on the Bogazköy gendarme station on 1 November 1992. Although noting that there was some uncertainty as to the exact date when the nine houses were burnt, it accepted the applicants' claims that this occurred on 10 November 1992.

facts.text: No proper investigation was carried out at the domestic level regarding the destruction of the nine houses at Kelekçi on 10 November 1992, either immediately after or thereafter.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission found that no proper investigation was carried out at the domestic level regarding the destruction of the nine houses at Kelekçi on 10 November 1992 either immediately after the event or thereafter.

facts.text: A gendarmerie report of 29 November 1993 and other incident reports did not result in any investigation or attempt to establish responsibility for the destruction.

anchor.surface_text: Apparently, a gendarmerie report of 29 November 1993 dealt with events at Kelekçi.  However, the Commission concluded that this report and other "incident reports" which had been submitted to the Chief Public Prosecutor at the Diyarbakir State Security Court, in so far as they concerned the destruction of the nine houses, did not result in any investigation of the facts and involved no attempt to establish responsibility for the destruction.

facts.text: Applicants lost their homes but received no proper advice or assistance on how to obtain compensation or other forms of aid.

anchor.surface_text: It was also established by the Commission that, although the applicants had lost their homes, no one gave proper advice to them or, apparently, to the other displaced Kelekçi villagers, on how to obtain compensation for the loss of their homes or other forms of assistance.

facts.text: Petitions were made by the mayor and statements given to State officials, but no authority took up the applicants' problems or referred them to the competent body.

anchor.surface_text: Petitions were made by the mayor of the village and statements were given to several State officials.  However, no authority took up the applicants' problems or referred them to the competent body.

facts.text: Certain applicants or persons believed to be applicants, such as Hüseyin Akdivar and Ahmet Çiçek, were questioned by State authorities about their applications to the Commission.

anchor.surface_text: There was also evidence before the Commission that, after the case had been brought to it, certain of the applicants, or persons who were believed to be applicants such as Hüseyin Akdivar and Ahmet Çiçek (see paragraphs 48-50 below), had been questioned by the State authorities about their applications to the Commission.

facts.text: A filmed interview was provided with these two persons, during which they were asked about the case in Strasbourg.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission had been provided with a filmed interview with these two persons, during which they were asked about the case in Strasbourg.

facts.text: Investigation reports and recorded statements by villagers submitted by the Government were dated September 1994, almost two years after the destruction of the nine houses.

anchor.surface_text: As regards the events on 10 November 1992 (see paragraph 15 above), the Commission noted that the investigation reports and the recorded statements by villagers which had been submitted to it by the respondent Government were dated September 1994, i.e. almost two years after the destruction of the nine houses.

facts.text: In these statements, villagers blamed the PKK for setting fire to the houses; the inquiry took place after further damage to the village and after the Commission had communicated complaints to the Government.

anchor.surface_text: In these statements they placed the blame on the PKK for setting fire to the houses.  At that time, a number of villagers had been heard by the authorities about events at Kelekçi.  It was observed that this inquiry had taken place at a time when the village had been further damaged on 6 April 1993, and after the Commission had communicated the applicants' complaints to the Government for observations and decided to hold an oral hearing in the case.

facts.text: The investigation reports of September 1994 were based on a helicopter mission on 21 September 1994, during which the team did not land but observed the village from low-level flights.

anchor.surface_text: It was further noted that the investigation reports of September 1994 were based on an exploratory mission undertaken by helicopter on 21 September 1994.  During this mission, the investigating team did not land at Kelekçi but only observed the village during low-level flights.

facts.text: The report stated that all houses at Kelekçi had collapsed and there were no inhabitants in the village.

anchor.surface_text: The report stated that all the houses at Kelekçi had collapsed and that there were no inhabitants in the village.

facts.text: A team of gendarmes heard villagers in April 1993, but their statements did not reference the incident of 10 November 1992 and appeared stereotyped and uniform.

anchor.surface_text: As to the events of 6 April 1993, the Commission found that a team of gendarmes had heard various villagers in April 1993.  However, in their recorded statements no reference was made by the villagers to the incident of 10 November 1992.  The statements were examined by the Commission in order to determine whether they should affect the Commission's findings on questions of fact in respect of the incident complained of.

facts.text: The Commission concluded that the statements gave the impression of being drafted by gendarmes rather than spontaneous, and some contradicted other statements by the same persons.

anchor.surface_text: In its report of 26 October 1995 it concluded as follows: "197. In this respect, it is striking that the various statements by the villagers are drafted in a stereotyped form and have on the whole the same contents ... Thus it seems highly doubtful whether the recorded statements to the gendarmes can be said to reflect the information that the villagers intended to convey in regard to the events at issue."

facts.text: The Commission attached no particular weight to the villagers' April 1993 statements and noted the inadequacy of domestic investigations into the destruction of the homes.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission concluded that it attached no particular weight to the statements of the villagers in April 1993.  It further noted the inadequacy of any real investigations at the domestic level which could be of assistance in elucidating the events on 10 November 1992.

facts.text: In the absence of relevant domestic investigations, the Commission based its findings on oral and written evidence submitted during proceedings before it.

anchor.surface_text: In the absence of any relevant investigations at the domestic level, the Commission based its finding on the evidence which had been given orally by various persons or submitted in writing in the course of the proceedings before it.

facts.text: The Commission found no evidence of conspiracy by villagers to accuse the State falsely to obtain compensation.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission concluded that there was no evidence of any conspiracy between the villagers to accuse the State of the burning of the houses in order to obtain compensation or for any other purpose.

facts.text: While security forces were in the village, no witness stated that any stranger was seen on 10 November 1992, and no evidence showed terrorists were present that day.

anchor.surface_text: It also noted that, while there was evidence that the security forces were in the village, none of the witnesses stated that any stranger had been seen at Kelekçi on 10 November 1992.  It was unlikely that terrorists would have set fire to nine houses in the village without anyone having noted their presence.  Nor was there any other evidence showing that terrorists had been at Kelekçi on that day.

facts.text: The Commission found convincingly that security forces were responsible for burning the nine Kelekçi houses on 10 November 1992.

anchor.surface_text: Following an assessment of the evidence, the Commission found it convincingly shown that security forces - presumably under the strain of intense terrorist activity in the area - were responsible for the burning of the nine Kelekçi houses on 10 November 1992.

facts.text: It was not shown that the applicants were forcibly expelled from Kelekçi, but loss of their homes caused them to abandon the village and move elsewhere.

anchor.surface_text: However, it had not been shown that the applicants were forcibly expelled from Kelekçi, but the loss of their homes caused them to abandon the village and move elsewhere.
